condition: nocturnal pruritus with tiny wavy threadlike burrows on the wrists and in the finger webs over 3 weeks shared with a household roommate
level_rationale: Three weeks of tiny wavy lines on the wrists and between the fingers shared with a household roommate and accompanied by itching that keeps a 22-year-old adult lying awake at night describes classic contagious interdigital ectoparasitic infestation warranting an outpatient clinic visit for diagnostic confirmation and prescription topical or oral treatment of both household contacts rather than over-the-counter self-care or emergency care, whereas hot swelling locking the fingers bent today signals acute pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis complicating scratched interdigital burrows and requiring immediate emergency department parenteral antibiotics and surgical hand evaluation.

design_note: Four atomic reference facts cover age 22, a roommate sharing the rash, 3 weeks of tiny wavy lines on the wrists and between the fingers, and nocturnal itching preventing sleep without naming scabies, with a 2-word span difference (24 vs 26 words) and zero contractions. Preserving the shared roommate rash context under Rule A and Rule D, replacing f4 at the existing fingers with hot swelling locking the fingers bent today shifts care unambiguously from clinic treatment (level 2) to emergency hand evaluation (level 4).
